replies.text:
Plain English-

In plain English: X (formerly Twitter) just made a change to stop a specific kind of bot spam.

The announcement from @XDevelopers means:

- If you're using their API (the tool developers use to post tweets automatically/programmatically) on the cheaper/free tiers (Free, Basic, Pro, or Pay-Per-Use plans),
- You can no longer use code to auto-reply to just any random post anymore.
- The only replies your bot/program is now allowed to post are:
  - When the original poster @mentions you in their tweet, or
  - When the original poster quotes one of your tweets/posts.

Regular manual replies (typing them yourself) are completely unaffected.  
Also, normal tweets (not replies) posted via the API still work the same way.

Why did they do this?  
To cut down on automated reply spam the annoying bot replies you see under popular posts (fake Elon accounts, crypto pumps, "follow me" bots, sugar daddy scams, AI-generated nonsense, etc.).

Who still can do whatever they want?  
Big/enterprise customers and special "Public Utility" apps are exempt they didn't get restricted.

Developer reactions (from the replies and quotes):
- Some people are happy it's tackling spam.
- Others think most of the worst bots aren't even using the official API anyway (they use scraping, browser automation, hacked accounts, etc.), so this won't fix the flood of garbage replies.
- A few are joking/sad that fake engagement farms or auto-reply "growth" tools just got nerfed.
- There's still frustration that human-looking bots and instant fake replies/likes keep appearing under big accounts.

Bottom line for a normal user like you:  
You probably won't notice much direct change.  
But if you post something popular, you should see slightly fewer obvious bot replies under it in the coming days/weeks (though plenty of other spam methods still exist).

If you're a developer building something on the API that relied on mass auto-replies → time to rethink the strategy or upgrade to Enterprise. 😅
